works.name: Rock 'n' Roll With The Modern Lovers

podcast.title: Anti-Hippie Image
podcast.body: Richman deliberately bucked the trends of his era by wearing his hair short when most male rockers sported long hair, openly reveling in his anti-hippie stance and embracing a distinct individuality. "He was also someone who at a time when every male rocker and every male rock fan wore their hair long, but this guy, nope, he wanted to wear his hair short. He was vehemently anti-hyppy and he reveled in being different."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

podcast.title: Contemporary Powerpop Sound
podcast.body: Recorded in 1972, their song "Roadrunner" is noted for sounding "every bit as modern powerpop as anything by the strokes or slone, the new pranographers, the Danny Warhol's, Jimmy Eat World, and even the Go-Ghosts, and the knack and blondie and the Romantics," demonstrating its ahead-of-its-time quality. "It was recorded in 1972, and it is every bit as modern powerpop as anything by the strokes or slone, the new pranographers, the Danny Warhol's, Jimmy Eat World, and even the Go-Ghosts, and the knack and blondie and the Romantics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

podcast.title: Groundwork for Punk Rock
podcast.body: The stripped-down songs of Jonathan Richman and The Modern Lovers were instrumental in laying the groundwork for punk rock, with their music frequently classified as proto-punk, meaning it predated and helped define the genre. "His stripped down songs help set the groundwork for punk rock. In fact, we classify his music as proto-punk, the stuff that had to happen first before punk rock could be born."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

podcast.title: Influence on Punk and Post-Punk
podcast.body: Although Jonathan Richman and the Modern Lovers never achieved significant record sales, they were highly influential to early punk bands and many post-punk groups such as the Sex Pistols, R.E.M., Violent Femmes, Dinosaur Jr., The Cars, The Pixies, and the Ramones. This impact stemmed from Jonathan Richman being a big Velvet Underground fan. "Jonathan Richmond and the Modern Lovers never sold a lot of records, but they were very important to the early punks and many of the post-punk bands like the Sex Pistols and REM and the Violent Femmes and Dinosaur Jr. and the Cars and the Pixies and the Ramones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 1

podcast.title: Movie Appearance - There's Something About Mary
podcast.body: Jonathan Richman made notable appearances in the movie "There's Something About Mary," where he was featured as the guitarist who pops up in various strange places throughout the film. "And if you remember the movie, there's something about Mary. Jonathan is the guy with a guitar who shows up in strain places during the film."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Peaked Too Soon - Bands That Were Ahead of Their Time

podcast.title: Velvet Underground Fanatic
podcast.body: Jonathan Richman was a "hardcore velvet underground fan," directly inspired by their music to pursue a career in music himself. "Jonathan Richmond was inspired to get into music because, like I said, of the Velvet Underground."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
